input.terminal_arc_rules: No arc enters source or leaves sink; source-to-sink arcs are allowed.
input.null_pointer_behavior: Null input returns -1 at declared lengths 0 and 50.

algorithm_profile.method: Sequential S-ARD: fixed ascending region order; staged local augmenting paths to the sink and eligible boundary vertices; region relabel after each discharge.
algorithm_profile.initialization: Saturate all source-outgoing arcs into a preflow, set all labels to 0 except source label d_infinity=|B|, and retain global residual/excess state.
algorithm_profile.boundary: B is the set of nonterminal endpoints of positive-capacity inter-region arcs; B_R is the set of external nonterminal neighbors of region R.
algorithm_profile.region_network: For a discharge, use current global residual capacities on R union {s,t} and on R<->B_R arcs, but set incoming boundary-to-R residual capacities to zero; local augmentations update the global residual and excess arrays.
algorithm_profile.stages: For k=0..|B|, target T_k={sink} union {v in B_R | label[v]<k}; repeatedly choose a shortest residual path from an active vertex in R to T_k, scanning vertex IDs ascending, and augment its bottleneck/excess.
algorithm_profile.relabel: After the final stage, set each u in R to the minimum k for which u reaches T_k in the updated local residual network, or |B| if none; boundary labels remain unchanged.
algorithm_profile.schedule: Sequential sweeps visit region IDs ascending and repeat until no positive-excess vertex has label below |B|. Optional global-gap heuristics and disk/parallel execution are omitted.
algorithm_profile.sweep_bound: For B boundary vertices, S-ARD terminates in at most 2*B^2+1 sweeps; this bounded profile rejects only if that theorem-based limit is exceeded.
algorithm_profile.complexity: At most 2*B^2+1 sweeps; each sweep discharges K regions, each with B+1 nested-target stages. Each stage uses deterministic breadth-first augmenting paths on at most N vertices and M residual arc records; for fixed targets this is Edmonds-Karp-style O(N*M^2).
algorithm_profile.distinctness: Unlike global push-relabel, this performs path augmentation to nested sink/boundary target sets and relabels by region distance. Unlike block merging, it preserves one global preflow/residual state while discharging the fixed regions sequentially.
algorithm_profile.maximum_result_derivation: At most M=12 source-outgoing arc records each have capacity at most 7, so flow is at most 84.

oracle_method: Primary: deterministic sequential S-ARD with staged BFS path augmentation, boundary-to-region capacity suppression, global residual/excess updates, and region relabeling. Independent: enumerate all source-side subsets and compute the minimum directed cut capacity.

source.sections: Paper §4.1-4.3 and Alg. 1; technical report §4.2-4.3 (S-ARD), Statement 9 and Theorem 3.
source.reuse: Algorithm descriptions only. This is a deterministic in-memory bounded sequential S-ARD profile, not the paper's distributed/streaming implementation or P-ARD parallel schedule.
